stem.text: Why is the ionic radius of a sulfide ion larger than the ionic radius of a potassium ion?

A.text: Ionic radius always decreases with increasing atomic number.

B.text: Positive ions always have smaller radii than negative ions.

C.text: The potassium ion has more protons in its nucleus than the sulfide ion.

D.text: The sulfide ion is doubly charged; the potassium ion is singly charged.
